chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf ibn Umayrah al-Nakha'i, from Khaythamah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Everything is perishable but His Face.' He (peace be upon him) replied: It is His Religion. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) are the Religion of Allah, His Face and His Eye among His servants, His tongue with which He speaks, and His Hand over His creation. And we are the Face of Allah through which He is approached; we will remain among His servants as long as Allah has a 'viewing/consideration' (ru'yah) for them. I asked: And what is the 'viewing/consideration'? He said: Need (al-hajah). When Allah has no need for them, He removes us to Him and does what He pleases.
ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'Everything is perishable but His Face' mean according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the concept of *Wajh Allah* (Face of God) not merely as divine essence, but as the enduring vehicle of His religion and authority, identifying the Prophet, Imam Ali, and the subsequent Imams as the specific 'Face' through which God is approached. The term *Ru'yah* (need/needfulness) signifies the functional necessity of the Imams for guiding creation; their presence is contingent upon this divine purpose, and their eventual return to Allah marks the completion of their custodial role. This interpretation underscores the Shia doctrine of the Imams as the living, tangible manifestation of God's will and mercy among humanity.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. My father, may Allah have mercy on him, that Sa`d ibn `Ad Allah, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa on the authority of `Ali ibn Sayf on the authority of his brother alHasan ibn Sayf on the authority of his father Sayf ibn `Amirah al-Nakha`i on the authority of Khaythamah that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: Everything is perishable but He. He (AS) resplied: It is His Religion. The Messenger of Allah (sw) and the Commander of the Faithful (AS) are the Religion of Allah amongst His Servants, His Face, His Eyes, His tongue with which He speaks and the Hand with which He covers His Creation. We are the Face with which He bestows (His Blessings). We will remain in His Servants as long as Allah has any consideration [rawiyyah] for them. I enquired, “What is consideration [rawiyyah]? He (AS) explained, “Need [alhajah]. When Allah has no need for them He removes us from them, and does as He pleases.”
